_meta.provenance: Fifty newly authored, bank-attested seed items in standard Italian; no learner sentence or personal data is reproduced. Passato remoto forms were cross-checked against the vendored verbecc table where available.
_meta.register: Neutral news and professional Italian; the passato remoto subset uses historical/reporting-style clauses that are also structurally possible at the imperfetto.
_meta.language_policy: sentence, question, options, answer, and contrast_form are Italian; why is concise English metalinguistic feedback.
_meta.register_semantics: Passato remoto is taught as a bounded perfective narrative tense, common in historical/literary standard prose and still ordinary in some regional speech. It is not defined as objectively distant in time and is not presented as semantically more completed than passato prossimo.
_meta.validation_notes: Each reciprocal frame appears once at imperfetto and once at passato prossimo; ten additional passato-remoto rows contrast with the corresponding imperfetto. Apart from required auxiliary, clitic, participle agreement, and l’/la surface alternations, contrast_form changes only target verbal morphology. No time adverb, duration phrase, habitual-frequency expression, completion predicate, or surrounding event independently determines aspect.
